name: Oil and gas well and field operations
one_line: The operator-side record of one oil or gas well or field after a specific operational activity is proposed, authorized, carried out, measured and closed: drilling and workover activity reports, completion and end-of-operations records, actual wellbore schematics, well tests, production allocation and operational/environmental returns. The anchor is not oil-and-gas vocabulary; it is a labelled relation among a licence or permit, field/site, well or facility identifier, actual operational state or measured production, and reporting period. A permit application, design drawing, market report, invoice or regulator case does not activate this row by topic alone. Placeholder template (J-IND, full J-DEPTH): the field-less resource_operations schema keeps fields and dimension_order empty until R1c adjudicates its proposed operational vocabulary.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The resource_operations schema already proposes `site` for the operating place a record is about. This row adds evidence that an oil or gas field, lease area or platform is a site role, while Photos `location` remains where an image was captured. No oil-and-gas-specific synonym is proposed.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Unchanged from the schema proposal: useful first only in a multi-field or multi-installation corpus and otherwise flattened. Coordinates and exact surface locations remain content evidence, not branch labels.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled Field, Lease, Area, Block, Platform or Facility slot can be direct evidence; prose, filenames and coordinates remain possible because they may identify a regulator district, contractor base, delivery point or cited location.

proposed_fields.example: Lease OCS-G 12345 / approved drilling consent WONS-DRL-0042
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The resource_operations schema already proposes the holder-side permit, lease, licence, concession, quota or connection authority. Oil and gas supplies the concrete lease-and-well-consent case. The issuing authority's case is government evidence; the operator's enduring right and conditions are this schema role.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Unchanged from the schema proposal and subject to the same protection caveat: useful where several leases or consents coexist, but flatten when it exposes an infrastructure or concession identifier without retrieval benefit.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Validation requires a labelled lease, licence, permit or consent identifier joined to holder/operator, field or well, activity and effective conditions. Identifier patterns and authority catalogues belong to R2/R4; this row supplies no regex or gazetteer.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The resource_operations schema already proposes `asset` for a stable operating unit. This row demonstrates the well/wellbore, completion, platform and production-facility case. A well number is the operational thread across activity, completion, tests and production, not a new private `well_id` field.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Unchanged from the schema proposal. For this template it is normally the intelligible parent below site because daily activity, completion state, tests and production are all meaningless without the well or facility they describe.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Validation requires a well, wellbore or facility identifier in a labelled role slot, ideally corroborated across an approved permit, activity report and completion or production record. An API-shaped or serial-shaped token alone is never sufficient.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The resource_operations schema proposes `output_stream` because extraction and metered production are not necessarily manufactured products. This row adds the allocation case where oil, gas, condensate and produced-water roles must remain distinct. No petroleum-specific variant is proposed.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Unchanged from the schema proposal, but not recommended as a standing level here. It is useful only when one field's corpus genuinely separates materially different streams; quantities and units never become destination values.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Direct only from labelled production/allocation columns or report slots. A hydrocarbon word in prose, a product price, a fluid property or a filename remains possible because it can occur in engineering, finance, research and market material.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The resource_operations schema already proposes the period the operation or measured production is ABOUT. A drilling-report week and a production month are not filesystem `creation_date`, Finance `tax_year`, Academic `term` or Photos `capture_year`.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Unchanged from the schema proposal. It is optional below site and asset, never first: year-first would split one well's continuous operational history across calendar branches.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Validation requires a date or interval in a labelled Reporting Period, Operation Date, Production Month or Activity Week slot with well/field operational context. A filename date or filesystem timestamp remains possible.

proposed_fields.example: well activity report / completion report / production allocation
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The resource_operations schema proposes reuse of canonical `record_type`; this row adds named document functions verified by official operator reporting systems. R1c must widen one global document-function key if necessary, never add `oil_gas_record_type`.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Inherited from the canonical key if R1c makes it legal on resource_operations. It is the leaf below well and optional period; a form number is evidence for a value, not the value by itself.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled form title and matching slot structure may establish the document function. An isolated word such as report, log, completion or production and an extension cannot.

deterministic: a well activity report structure joining a labelled lease or field, well/wellbore identifier, operator and rig, reporting interval, actual well status, measured and true-vertical depth, operation summary, casing or liner progress and test/log activity

an end-of-operations or well completion report joining the approved well identifier to actual spud/total-depth/completion dates, final status, drilled intervals, casing/cement/completion equipment, perforations, tests, logs and attachments; planned values alone are excluded

a daily drilling, completion, workover or plugging log whose repeated rows join operation date/time, well and rig, depth/progress, activity code or narrative, non-productive-time reason, fluid or pressure observations and current well state
a well potential or periodic well-test record joining the well identifier and test interval to measured oil, gas and water rates, pressures, choke or test conditions and test disposition

a production allocation or operations report whose rows join lease/field, well or measurement point, production month, oil/gas/water stream roles, measured or allocated volumes, disposition or inventory roles and operator submission status

an actual wellbore schematic explicitly attached to an end-of-operations, completion, workover or abandonment record, with as-executed casing, cement, perforation, tubing and barrier locations; a free-standing revision-controlled design sheet remains engineering

an operator environmental or integrity return tied to a named well, field or facility and permit condition, with sampling or inspection point, parameter, method, result, unit, reporting period and corrective or submission status

a well operations consent/permit held with its approved activity and subsequent activity/completion record under the same well reference; an application or issued instrument without evidence of actual operation is never sufficient

an archive manifest exposing one well/field reference and several activity reports, directional surveys, logs, completion attachments and production members; manifests are inspected without unpacking to disk
a structured portal export whose labelled columns repeatedly join well/lease identifiers, actual activity or production status, dates and operator; portal branding and a filename alone do not fire

a well number, API-shaped number, lease number, permit number, facility code, rig name or asset tag outside a labelled role slot and supporting operational structure
a depth, pressure, rate, volume, unit, coordinate, date, status word or time-series column alone

an operator, regulator, contractor, field, basin, platform or facility name alone; the role ambiguity is the same defect 00 identifies for a university name

grouping_reasons: one well or wellbore across permit, spud, weekly/daily activity, completion, tests, production, intervention and abandonment
one field or lease across wells, measurement points, monthly production allocations, environmental returns and operator submissions
one bounded drilling, workover or plugging operation across plan, consent, daily reports, surveys, end-of-operations report and attachments

a sparse field image, email, calendar notice or vendor log may join an accepted well group without receiving the well, field, authority or period facts

template.why: Empty by binding contract: resource_operations declares no field rows under PR-6, so this template cannot serialize destination dimensions. Subject to R1c, the researched recommendation is site/field then asset/well then reporting_period then record_type, with operating_authority optional above the well where one corpus spans several leases or consents. This differs from the resource_operations schema default proposal of site → operating_authority → output_stream → reporting_period → record_type: oil/gas work is well-history-led, so the enduring well normally outranks output stream; production stream is search/allocation evidence unless a corpus genuinely separates oil, gas and water branches. It is not time-first: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." A year-first tree would split one well's drilling-to-abandonment history. The order remains a recommendation the user may reverse, remove, add or flatten.

collides_with.signal: Direction one — resource_operations.oil-gas-operations owns an as-executed wellbore state when the sheet is an identified attachment to completion, workover or end-of-operations evidence and its casing, cement, perforation, tubing and barrier positions record what was actually installed. Direction two — engineering.drawing-package owns the controlled sheet/version family when title-block identifier, revision history and issue/transmittal structure are the governing evidence and no actual operation attachment is established. Same fixture bytes: `Well-Schematic_BR-17_As-Completed_Rev0.pdf`; the words well and as-completed, the title block and the revision designator count for neither side alone.

Direction one — resource_operations.oil-gas-operations owns the holder-side approved drilling instrument only when the same well reference is independently joined to actual activity or completion records; a permit copy alone does not activate this row. Direction two — government.permit-licensing owns the deciding authority's continuing-permission case: application intake, assessment, representations, decision, register/renewal and adverse-power apparatus. Same fixture bytes: `BSEE-0123_APD_OCS-G-12345_A-17_Approved-with-Conditions.pdf`; the permit reference and issuing letterhead are printed on both copies and discriminate nothing.

Direction one — resource_operations.oil-gas-operations owns the operator-prepared return when labelled field/facility and permit-condition evidence joins measured results to the producing operation and no authority receipt, officer assessment or enforcement step appears. Direction two — government.environmental-regulation owns the authority-side received and assessed copy when return-register receipt, receiving-officer review, surveillance, incident or enforcement evidence is present. Same fixture bytes: `EPR-AB1234 - Quarterly Monitoring Return Q2 2026 - Outfall 001.xlsx`; the existing government neighbour assigns a generic operator copy to manufacturing.environmental-compliance, so R1c must reconcile that generic claim with this field-specific operator row rather than silently letting both stand.

Direction one — resource_operations.oil-gas-operations owns the report content that joins lease/field, well or measurement point, reporting month and oil/gas/water production or allocation roles, even when the operator later submits it. Direction two — business_operations.corporate-regulatory-filings owns the compelled-submission wrapper and trail: external obligation, deadline, filing reference, declaration, receipt, acknowledgement, reminder or penalty. Same fixture bytes: `OGOR-A_Well-Production_OCS-G-12345_2026-06.csv`; well/production rows support this row, while a submission receipt or authority acknowledgement supports the filing row, and neither may infer the other's evidence from custody alone.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone readable permit, well report, completion attachment or test record with durable value but no reliably evidenced well/field group belongs here rather than activating from a form number or oil-and-gas word.

Use when a file is operationally shaped but holder role or actual-versus-planned status cannot be settled: an unattributed monitoring workbook, marked-up schematic, daily report without labelled well identity or quantity table without allocation roles.
Native well-log formats, proprietary drilling databases, encrypted data rooms, damaged scans and unreadable portal backups keep basic metadata and must not acquire purpose from their filenames.
A field photograph with real camera evidence but no readable well, site or operational subject remains an image rather than an oil/gas record inferred from industrial appearance.

Market outlooks, published reserve reports, regulatory guidance and technical papers may be rich in oil/gas vocabulary and data but are reading material without an active operator-side well or field relation.

When an inactive file exposes precise well coordinates, subsurface configuration, critical-infrastructure details, incident narratives or commercially sensitive production/reserve data, protection is preferable to a topic guess. This is a residual recommendation, not a handling class.

sensitivity_why: Well and field records can expose precise infrastructure and subsurface locations, wellbore and barrier configuration, production and reserve performance, vulnerabilities, incident or non-productive-time narratives, environmental exceedances, lease/permit identifiers and commercially sensitive allocations. Some regulatory copies may later be public, but publication of one member does not lower the packet's posture. This row assigns only potentially_sensitive, no P7 handling class, and keeps coordinates, quantities, pressures, conditions and personal contacts out of destination dimensions and general summaries.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-OILGAS-1: does this well-history-led template survive as a distinct organizational situation once resource_operations' default template is finalized, or is oil and gas only a value set inside the schema default? Keep it if well-activity/completion recognition and site→well→period→record_type materially differ; refuse it if only vocabulary differs. NJ-OILGAS-2: should operator-side compelled production and environmental returns be owned by this sector template, by business_operations.corporate-regulatory-filings, or co-recommended from one shared P10 definition? The same bytes carry both content and submission purpose. NJ-OILGAS-3: is schema proposal `asset` broad enough for well and wellbore identity, and `site` broad enough for field/lease/platform, or does one of those roles require a canonical split? Do not mint `well_id` or `field` locally before R1c answers. NJ-OILGAS-4: the government environmental neighbour currently sends a generic operator monitoring copy to manufacturing.environmental-compliance; confirm that an oil/gas field return instead belongs here, or merge operator environmental compliance into one cross-sector applicability definition. NJ-OILGAS-5: should this template's precise infrastructure and subsurface material receive protection rules stronger than catalogue potentially_sensitive even when portions are on public registers? That is a P7 policy decision, not a handling class this row may invent.
